# CLI ⇄ shared summary schema

Canonical schema: `src/lib/summary-schema.ts` + `docs/summary-schema.md` on **feat/v2** (web worker), vendored
here from **5d3087a** (sha256 `06436fe94c80524600f55a3be8b5e0b1ac8f40490c6f74e0cd0ea0e60c117b24`).

* **Copy, not fork.** `cli/src/summary-schema.mjs` is generated by `node cli/scripts/vendor-schema.mjs <ref>`
  (esbuild strips the types; logic untouched) and pinned by commit and sha256 (`VENDORED_FROM`). A published npm
  package can't import from the web repo, so it ships the copy.
* `cli/src/summary.mjs` builds the `UsageSummary` and encodes only with the shared `encodeSummaryFit()`. The CLI has
  no shed logic of its own. Models past the 12 slots merge into `OTHER_ID` (`"other"`), and unmapped models into
  `{id: null}`; both merged entries sit at the end, after the per-id rows.
* Warn codes emitted: `retention-30d`, `codex-zst-skipped`, `opencode-sqlite-unavailable`, `no-token-data`,
  `unmapped-models`, `partial-window`, `codex-model-fallback`, `fuzzy-model-match`, `parse-errors`.
* Tests (`cli/test/schema.test.mjs`):
  * round-trip through the vendored copy (every Node);
  * the pinned commit hashes to the pinned sha (when the git repo is reachable);
  * on Node 22.18+, import the canonical `.ts` and check `decodeSummary` / `encodeSummaryFit` byte-for-byte.

## Prices

`data/prices.json` is the `tokenreceipt.prices/1` table exactly as `GET https://devprohacks.in/api/prices` serves it:
`{schema, asOf, generatedAt, rows[{id, label, kind, input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, aliases, compare}]}`, USD
per 1M tokens. It is generated from the price service's public snapshot, whose sources are vendor pricing pages,
LiteLLM and models.dev (both MIT) and vendor announcements. The generator refuses any other source.
